pr_title: lib: os: reboot: a few cleanups
pr_body:
After https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/62dbe72cb7ac55d1ae3ce62e5fb1fae47b9b293a and discussions in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/60626 I realized the reboot functionality required a bit of love. So I tried to clean up things a little bit. I may have made a few mistakes, so please, review. I tried to make changes in small steps to ease the review process.

Fixes #60915
pr_comments: The cleanup lgtm, however, I would put the fix for https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/60915 into its own PR
Major changes since last revision: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/60920/commits/b9ecbfcab85b4c16a6275f3c1cae3da38cb2150d (to be discussed in arch wg today)

Arch WG:

- @gmarull showed the cleanup in general
- @nashif looks at the changes in `sys/reboot.h` and states that we must be careful with changes like those. Also, looking at Linux is not always the right thing since it doesn't translate directly due to the complexity
- @carlescufi proposes keeping the `sys_reboot(enum )` API but adding a new `enum` option that is `DEFAULT`.
- @nashif suggests a single API for all operations. @gmarull has looked at the Linux kernel
- @ceolin asks if we have clarified what "cold" and "warm" means. @gmarull states that it depends on the platform
last push: introduced `SYS_REBOOT_DEFAULT` as discussed in the call
last push: added a missing CONFIG_REBOOT=y in task_wdt sample

we still have 2 changes that will possibly break out of tree implementations:
- Moving from weak symbol to requiring HAS_REBOOT
- Change of the name implementing the reboot code, i.e. `sys_arch_reboot()` to `z_sys_reboot()`

> we still have 2 changes that will possibly break out of tree implementations:
> 
> * Moving from weak symbol to requiring HAS_REBOOT

weak change is not related to HAS_REBOOT. This PR removes weaks usage in favor of Kconfig options so that non-standard C features are not used. HAS_REBOOT prevents selecting REBOOT if not implemented.

> * Change of the name implementing the reboot code, i.e. `sys_arch_reboot()` to `z_sys_reboot()`

this is done because reboot doesn’t seem to be arch specific only, also to clarify this is an internal API.


IMHO stability should be guaranteed for the public interface. If we want to keep stability even for internals, we’ll never evolve.

> IMHO stability should be guaranteed for the public interface. If we want to keep stability even for internals, we’ll never evolve.

I agree, and especially for architectures. Out-of-tree architectures are not supported by Zephyr.

> weak change is not related to HAS_REBOOT. This PR removes weaks usage in favor of Kconfig options so that non-standard C features are not used. HAS_REBOOT prevents selecting REBOOT if not implemented.

that is what I mean, you are removing weak usage in favor of Kconfig (`Moving from weak symbol to requiring HAS_REBOOT`), so an SoC implementation using the weak function and without HAS_REBOOT will break.

> this is done because reboot doesn’t seem to be arch specific only, also to clarify this is an internal API.

It is a hook someone can implement in their platform, This is not a classic internal API. This is more like `arch_` and `soc_` calls we have in various places.

> I agree, and especially for architectures. Out-of-tree architectures are not supported by Zephyr.

Who said anything about out of tree architectures? This functional is usually implemented by platforms or SoCs. Look at this PR, most of the changes are in SOC code implementing this feature.

Anyways, I know most of this is special in many ways, but I do not see anything in this PR documenting or at least trying to help or mitigate breakage. This is one more thing that will break and make migration to a new release more painful for out of tree users.

> > weak change is not related to HAS_REBOOT. This PR removes weaks usage in favor of Kconfig options so that non-standard C features are not used. HAS_REBOOT prevents selecting REBOOT if not implemented.
> 
> that is what I mean, you are removing weak usage in favor of Kconfig (`Moving from weak symbol to requiring HAS_REBOOT`), so an SoC implementation using the weak function and without HAS_REBOOT will break.

Not really. It is true that now implementers of the hook need to select HAS_REBOOT, if not, CONFIG_REBOOT is not selectable. This kind of pattern is followed in a few other places to avoid linking errors when a feature is not implemented. About weaks, what has been done is to introduce specific options if certain archs need to support SoC-specific hooks (the case of ARM, and POSIX likely to ease some testing).

> 
> > this is done because reboot doesn’t seem to be arch specific only, also to clarify this is an internal API.
> 
> It is a hook someone can implement in their platform, This is not a classic internal API. This is more like `arch_` and `soc_` calls we have in various places.

`sys_arch_reboot` was an internal API, never meant to be used by application code. Note that it was not documented, and no declaration existed in any header (reboot.c just declared it internally).

> 
> > I agree, and especially for architectures. Out-of-tree architectures are not supported by Zephyr.
> 
> Who said anything about out of tree architectures? This functional is usually implemented by platforms or SoCs. Look at this PR, most of the changes are in SOC code implementing this feature.
> 
> Anyways, I know most of this is special in many ways, but I do not see anything in this PR documenting or at least trying to help or mitigate breakage. This is one more thing that will break and make migration to a new release more painful for out of tree users.

I can add an extra commit updating release notes, I tend to update them before release though.

> > I agree, and especially for architectures. Out-of-tree architectures are not supported by Zephyr.
> 
> Who said anything about out of tree architectures? This functional is usually implemented by platforms or SoCs. Look at this PR, most of the changes are in SOC code implementing this feature.

Fair enough, but the rename makes sense, since this is not arch-specific as you point out.

> Not really. It is true that now implementers of the hook need to select HAS_REBOOT, if not, CONFIG_REBOOT is not selectable.

which is it? this is a conflicting staement. if architecture does not select HAS_REBOOT and I have implemented a custom reboot using the weak function, I end up with my application building with reboot disabled, so this is bad.

if HAS_REBOOT is selected by someone, i.e. architecture, I will get reboot functionality but my application and platform will be using different code than the one I have implemented out of tree, i.e. no warning or complaints and users wondering what went wrong....

> `sys_arch_reboot` was an internal API, never meant to be used by application code. Note that it was not documented, and no declaration existed in any header (reboot.c just declared it internally).

Not application code, correct. but it is a hook a platform can implement. I think this is a class of interfaces we need to differentate from classic internal functions.  Not something I would treat like  public APIs and the policy around them, but it should be dealt with differently. Something to discuss somewhere else I guess.

> > Not really. It is true that now implementers of the hook need to select HAS_REBOOT, if not, CONFIG_REBOOT is not selectable.
> 
> which is it? if architecture does not select HAS_REBOOT and I have implemented a custom reboot using the weak function, I end up with my application building with reboot disabled, so this is bad.

Architecture will select HAS_REBOOT only if it provides a valid hook. So if it didn't, your code will still work provided you now select HAS_REBOOT in your own hook, regardless of weak usage. HAS_REBOOT is required, yes, but I think it is being added to solve another problem (linking errors for those not implementing reboot). The only problem may come if your arch supported weaks, but now relies on a Kconfig to explicitly choose a custom hook (ARM/POSIX). This is again to avoid usage of non-standard C features. It is a matter of documenting the changes in the release notes, and offering some quick migration tips.
 
> 
> if HAS_REBOOT is selected by someone, i.e. architecture, I will get reboot functionality but my application and platform will be using different code than the one I have implemented out of tree, i.e. no warning or complaints and users wondering what went wrong....
> 
> > `sys_arch_reboot` was an internal API, never meant to be used by application code. Note that it was not documented, and no declaration existed in any header (reboot.c just declared it internally).
> 
> Not application code, correct. but it is a hook a platform can implement. I think this is a class of interfaces we need to differentate from classic internal functions. Not some I would compare to public APIs and the policy around them, but it should be dealt with differently. Something to discuss somewhere else I guess.

As I said, I think internals should not be part of stability guarantees. I'd apply the same for drivers, actually. It is a very different scenario to be a driver interface user than a driver implementer. For example, a driver class may decide to gather 2 driver ops into a single one, but keep the same public interface. If doing oot drivers, you should be prepared to deal with such internal changes, otherwise take some time to upstream your code. In this particular case, the interface wasn't even exposed in any header, nor documented. I think stability concerns are sometimes going too far, making simple changes too difficult.
last push: added CONFIG_REBOOT_NO_ARCH (to replace arch weaks in a generic way) and added release notes detailing all changes

issue_context.title: Remove `pm_system_reset` and use `sys_reboot` instead for PSCI
issue_context.body:
Commit https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/62dbe72cb7ac55d1ae3ce62e5fb1fae47b9b293a introduced a new API, `pm_system_reset`, that currently uses PSCI under the hood to implement a system reset.

But we already have `sys_reboot()`, which supports implementing custom hooks, and exposes the exact same functionality.
Therefore, `pm_system_reset()` must be removed and instead a new hook/backend for `sys_reboot()` using PSCI must be added.

This is indeed how it is also done in Linux, where the reboot functionality is handled by the file `reboot.h`, and hooks/handlers can be added dynamically:
https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.4.4/source/include/linux/reboot.h#L49
A PSCI handler is then registered and used with the `reboot.h` API:
https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.4.4/source/drivers/firmware/psci/psci.c#L308
https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.4.4/source/drivers/firmware/psci/psci.c#L626

review_comments:
Not trying to open an endless discussion, but: 
> Cold reboot is basically what you expect to happen on powering up a device;

Agreed.

> warm reset may be..

..a lot of different things, and for HW reboots triggered by SW, the HW may provide several options with significantly different outcomes.
Which makes me wonder if Zephyr should not make it easier for platforms to define their own different reboot types. This is probably out of scope for this PR, though this enum seems to be tying things up?

I think it's easy to agree on what cold boot means, but not so much on "warm". I'm not even sure we're now able to support something like warm reset properly, see, for example, https://trustedfirmware-a.readthedocs.io/en/latest/design/reset-design.html

reboot types have been undocumented from day 0 https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/826edfc16b2615e8ee5f8fd0b06af39ded365a8e, who knows what they meant in 2016...
I may be missing something, but instead of removing this, shouldn't we select HAS_REBOOT from ARCH_POSIX, and keep this (now named `z_sys_reboot()`)
I guess it's ok to allow posix implementation to shut the application down because it cannot reboot, then? A reboot in posix would be like `sys_reboot()` + relaunch zephyr manually?

Yep, this default reboot hook is just terminating returning 1 to the invoking shell after printing a descriptive message. A board, or app developer can override that with something else.
Normally a reboot is the result of a failure; And in an environment like this, terminating by default is reasonable.
please check latest revision. I've removed `__weak` (non-standard feature_ in favor of a Kconfig option (like ARM)
